issue.title: Flaky test_creation_budget_defers_then_converges_next_pass: 90s work_seconds budget races under full parallel load
issue.description: tests/test_external_mirror_issues.py::test_creation_budget_defers_then_converges_next_pass asserts an exact 25/15 beads_created split across two passes of run_issue_mirror_for_project, relying on _MirrorBudget's default work_seconds=90.0 wall-clock deadline (src/sase/external_mirror/issues.py _apply(), checked via time.monotonic() >= work_deadline) never being hit for 40 trivial in-memory FakeIssueProvider issues. Observed failing during 'just test-scoped' under the full ~29157-test scoped selection triggered by an unrelated sase.schema.json/default_config.yml change (630s wall time total); the same test call took 97.69s in that run per pytest's slowest-durations report, vs 0.18s when run in isolation immediately after ('.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_external_mirror_issues.py::test_creation_budget_defers_then_converges_next_pass -q' => 1 passed in 1.82s). This is a live reproducible flake caused by real-wall-clock CPU contention under heavy parallel test execution, not a logic bug. Fix: make the budget/deadline injectable (e.g. a monotonic clock callable) so tests can assert exact split behavior deterministically without depending on real elapsed wall-clock time, following the pattern already used elsewhere in this repo for similar timing-window flakes (e.g. sase-gs).

evidence.note: Proposed by phase sase-k0.4.2 during task-gate convergence landing at HEAD 9960d7444: the post-test flake-baseline gate independently named tests/test_external_mirror_issues.py::test_creation_budget_defers_then_converges_next_pass, while the exact node passed in isolation. The epic changes task-gate convergence/config and does not touch the mirror budget's wall-clock deadline mechanism.

Independently hit while landing epic sase-k3 (phase sase-k3.6) on a clean master 1f388edee after 'just install': 'just check-full' passed every lint gate, SASE validation, committed plans, and the full pytest cost lane plus its suite-cost budgets, then failed ONLY 'flake baseline'. tests/test_external_mirror_issues.py::test_creation_budget_defers_then_converges_next_pass was among the 7 nodes exceeding tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt. Same scope caveat as my sase-jq +1: the node did not fail live in my run (the full lane was green); the gate named it from the shared durable full-run record pool. Continued-impact evidence — the gate blocks check-full on a clean, unrelated tree — not a fresh live reproduction. This phase made no source changes.

Recurrence during epic sase-k2's landing (agent sase-k2.land, workspace sase_13, HEAD 67d846327): this node was the 7th of 7 named by 'just check-full's flake-baseline gate, alongside sase-jq's six. The full pytest lane itself was green, so this is gate/durable-record impact rather than a live failure.

CORRECTION FOR WHOEVER WORKS THIS: the description's stated mechanism is stale against master. It says the test relies on '_MirrorBudget's default work_seconds=90.0' and cites a 97.69s observed duration exceeding it. Epic sase-k2's phase sase-k2.3 landed fb33e3c1f at 12:09:52 EDT on 2026-08-12 -- 25 minutes BEFORE this bead was filed at 12:34 -- replacing 'work_seconds: float = 90.0' with 'work_seconds: float = 0.75 * LANE_CHOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS' in src/sase/external_mirror/issues.py:131, where LANE_CHOP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300.0 (src/sase/external_mirror/budget.py, matching the external_mirror lane's chop_timeout: 5m). The effective deadline on master is therefore 225s, not 90s. sase-k2.2's workspace evidently branched before fb33e3c1f, so it measured the old value.

The 97.69s datapoint no longer exceeds the budget, which likely removes the specific race that was observed -- but it does not close the bead: the test still asserts an exact 25/15 split against a real time.monotonic() wall-clock deadline, so it remains contention-sensitive at a higher threshold. The requested fix (inject the clock so the split is deterministic) still stands, and re-measuring against 225s before deciding is worth one step.

Proposed by phase sase-jx.5.5.2 during finish_jx5_landing closeout: tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake at b4c6038e6 reported seven nodes over tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt after just check-full passed the full non-visual test-cost lane. One node was tests/test_external_mirror_issues.py::test_creation_budget_defers_then_converges_next_pass, matching this task's contention-sensitive mirror budget split. The epic diff was AXE chop-overrun docs/dependency/golden landing work and does not touch external mirror issue budgeting.

Independently reproduced while landing epic sase-ko (land agent sase-ko.land) on master 7e8f528b2 after 'just install'. 'just selection-health --fail-on-new-flake' exits 1 with tests/test_external_mirror_issues.py::test_creation_budget_defers_then_converges_next_pass among the 7 nodes exceeding tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt, while an isolated rerun of the whole file passes (74 nodes across test_contract_manifest.py/test_core_vcs_log.py/test_external_mirror_issues.py passed in 22.69s). Epic sase-ko changes only AXE chop guard preflight (agent_runners provider, run_every cadence on guard skips) and never touches _MirrorBudget's wall-clock work_seconds deadline. Surfaced as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on phase bead sase-ko.2.
